# Prism

One change goes in, separate bands come out.

Prism is a review dashboard for people with many changes in progress across many projects. It splits each change into four categories so you can read the parts you care about first:

- **spec**: design docs, RFCs, markdown
- **prod**: production code
- **test**: tests
- **other**: config, CI, lockfiles, everything else

Every category is shown as an inline diff. Markdown is **rendered**, with insertions and deletions marked inside the rendered text, so spec changes read like a marked-up document instead of a raw patch.

## Core idea: `BulkDelta`

The root type is a `BulkDelta`: a set of changes on a branch compared with its base. A change doesn't have to be a PR yet:

| Has a local checkout | Has a PR | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yes | no | a worktree you're hacking in, or one an agent is working in |
| no | yes | a PR you opened from another machine, not checked out here |
| yes | yes | the usual case |

```ts
interface BulkDelta {
  id: DeltaId;               // "owner/repo:branch"
  repo: RepoKey;
  branch: string | null;     // null = detached HEAD
  base: { ref: string; sha: string };
  title: string;             // PR title, else the last commit subject, else the branch name

  local: LocalCheckout | null;   // path, head commit, uncommitted counts, commits not yet pushed
  pr: PullRequest | null;        // number, url, state, headSha
  surfaces: SurfaceRef[];        // Dormouse panes working on it (live, never saved)

  source: 'local' | 'pr';    // where the diff comes from
}
```

The full model is in [`src/types.ts`](src/types.ts).

### Decisions

- **The id stays the same when a PR is opened.** It's `owner/repo:branch`, so a local-only delta and its later PR are the same entry, and focus settings (pinned or muted) carry over. Repos with no GitHub remote use the clone's path instead of `owner/repo`.
- **The local checkout wins when both exist.** The diff comes from the working tree, so it includes uncommitted edits and commits you haven't pushed. `FileChange.committed` marks changes that exist only on disk.
- **Choosing the base:** if there's a PR, use its base branch. Otherwise use the merge-base with `origin/<default branch>`.
- **Summary and detail are separate.** `DeltaSummary` has only per-category counts, so the dashboard loads quickly. `DeltaDetail` has the hunks and markdown contents, and is fetched when you open a delta.
- **Markdown is diffed block by block.** Each paragraph, heading, list item, code fence, or table is a block. Blocks that changed are then diffed word by word. Because each block is rendered as its own unit, `<ins>`/`<del>` tags can't break markdown syntax. Rendering needs both full versions of the file, not just the patch.
- **Categories come from glob rules.** Rules are checked in order and the first match wins: `foo.spec.ts` is a test, while `specs/foo.md` is a spec. Rules can be overridden per repo in `PrismState.rulesByRepo`.

## Discovery

Prism builds its list of deltas from two sources and joins them on `id`:

1. **Local:** for each clone under `scanRoots` (e.g. `~/projects`), `git remote get-url origin` gives the `owner/repo` and `git worktree list --porcelain` gives each worktree's branch. Worktrees that have changes compared with their base become deltas. Clean checkouts are skipped.
2. **GitHub:** `gh search prs --author=@me --state=open`.

### Dormouse integration

Prism runs inside Dormouse, and each delta shows which Dormouse surfaces are working on it, taken from `dor list --json --all`:

- Terminals and tools match when their `cwd` is the delta's `local.path` or a folder inside it. The longest matching path wins, so worktrees inside the main clone get their own surfaces.
- Browsers match when their `url` starts with the PR's URL.
- `needsAttention` (the surface is ringing or marked todo) lets the dashboard put deltas where an agent is waiting on you at the top.

Prism itself should run as a Dormouse surface: `dor ensure -- bun run dev`, then `dor agent-browser open surface:N`.

## Saved state

`~/.prism/state.json` (`PrismState`) holds focus per delta, per-repo category rules, category order, which categories start collapsed, and `scanRoots`. Surfaces and GitHub data are never saved; they're rebuilt on every refresh.

## Known gaps

- PRs from two forks with the same branch name (e.g. `patch-1`) get the same id. That's fine while we only show your own PRs.
- `git diff <base>` leaves out files git doesn't track yet. They have to be found separately with `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`.
- The default rules treat every `.md` file as a spec, including README and CHANGELOG.

## Stack (planned)

TypeScript on Bun, served as a local web page.

- `picomatch` for globs
- `diff` (jsdiff) for line and word diffs
- `marked` or `remark` to split and render markdown blocks
- `parse-diff` for unified patches

## Next steps

1. `discover.ts`: find local worktrees and PRs, join them into `BulkDelta[]`, and attach surfaces.
2. `classify.ts`: apply the category rules to each `FileChange`.
3. `diff.ts`: code hunks and block-by-block markdown diffs.
4. A dashboard page listing deltas, and a detail page per delta with collapsible category sections.

# priδm

One change goes in, separate bands come out.

priδm is a review dashboard for people with many changes in progress across many projects. It splits each change into categories so you can read the parts you care about first. The defaults are:

- **spec**: design docs, RFCs, markdown
- **prod**: production code
- **test**: tests
- **other**: everything else

You can define your own categories per repo. `other` is the only built-in one.

Every category is shown as an inline diff. Markdown is **rendered**, with insertions and deletions marked inside the rendered text, so spec changes read like a marked-up document instead of a raw patch.

priδm runs inside Dormouse and shows which Dormouse panes (agents, dev servers, browsers) are working on each change.

## Specs

- [**Implementation plan**](specs/plan.md): phases, time boxes, and what to cut if we run late
- **Architecture**
  - [Data model](specs/architecture/model.md): `BulkDelta`, ids, local vs. PR
  - [Categories](specs/architecture/categories.md): glob rules keyed by origin
  - [Discovery](specs/architecture/discovery.md): finding worktrees, PRs, and Dormouse surfaces
  - [Diffs](specs/architecture/diffs.md): Monaco for code, a merged document in MDXEditor for markdown
- **UI**
  - [Viewing a delta](specs/ui/viewing.md): collapsed categories and what loads when
  - [Design](specs/ui/design.md): Primer, and one set of diff colors for code and markdown
  - [Storybook](specs/ui/storybook.md): every component in every state
- [Stack](specs/stack.md): libraries, project layout, pitfalls

The types everything is built on are in [`src/types.ts`](src/types.ts).

# Categories

Every changed file is in exactly one category. Categories are just names you define. The only built-in one is `other`, for files that match nothing. The default rules define `spec`, `prod`, and `test`, but they're ordinary categories you can rename, remove, or add to.

Which category a file belongs to depends only on its path: the new path, or the old path for a deleted file. So it doesn't matter which two commits are being compared.

## Rules, keyed by origin

Each origin has its own globs in `~/.pridm/categories.json`, which you edit by hand:

```json
{
  "*": {
    "spec": ["**/spec/**", "**/specs/**", "**/*.md"],
    "test": ["**/test/**", "**/tests/**", "**/*.test.*"],
    "prod": ["**/*.{ts,js,go,py,java,kt}"]
  },
  "github.com/diffplug/spotless": {
    "spec": ["**/spec/**"],
    "test": ["**/test/**"],
    "migrations": ["**/db/migrations/**"],
    "prod": ["**/src/main/**"]
  }
}
```

- Categories are checked in the order they're written, and the first one with a matching glob wins. In the `*` entry, `test/README.md` is a spec, because `spec` comes first. Put `test` first if you'd rather it were a test, but then tests are also the first section.
- A file that matches nothing is `other`. You can also list `other` yourself, to claim files before a later, broader category does (e.g. `"other": ["**/generated/**"]` before `"prod": ["**"]`).
- The sections of a delta appear in the same order as its origin's categories, with `other` last. Categories with no changed files are left out.
- `*` applies to every origin without its own entry. An origin's entry replaces `*` completely; the two aren't merged, so you can read an origin's rules in one place.
- Keying by origin matters because conventions differ: in a Ruby repo, `spec/` holds RSpec tests, not design docs.

The defaults are `DEFAULT_CATEGORIES` in [`src/types.ts`](../../src/types.ts). Origins are normalized as described in the [data model](model.md#decisions).

## Known gaps

- The default rules treat every `.md` file as a spec, including README and CHANGELOG.

# Diffs

For every file, the server sends both full versions: `original` and `modified`. Code goes to Monaco, and markdown goes to MDXEditor as one merged document.

## Code: Monaco `DiffEditor`

- Inline view: `renderSideBySide: false`.
- Unchanged regions folded: `hideUnchangedRegions: { enabled: true }`.
- Read-only.
- Monaco computes the diff itself, which is why the server sends full versions, not hunks.
- The language comes from the file extension.

## Markdown: a merged document in MDXEditor

MDXEditor's own diff mode (`diffSourcePlugin`, checked in v4.5.0) is a CodeMirror `MergeView` that shows the markdown **source** side by side. It's neither rendered nor inline, so we don't use it.

What MDXEditor does give us: its core plugin parses and renders `~~strikethrough~~` and `==highlight==`. So the server builds one merged markdown document:

- deleted text becomes `~~deleted~~`
- inserted text becomes `==inserted==`

We show that document in a read-only MDXEditor in rich-text mode, and CSS colors deletions red and insertions green.

### Building the merged document

1. Parse both versions into top-level blocks with `mdast-util-from-markdown`: paragraph, heading, list item, block quote, code block, table, thematic break.
2. Diff the two lists of blocks by their source text (jsdiff `diffArrays`).
3. An unchanged block is copied as is.
4. An inserted or deleted block has its text wrapped in `==…==` or `~~…~~`, keeping its markdown prefix (`## `, `- `, `> `).
5. Within a run of changed blocks, blocks of the same type are lined up in order. A pair whose words mostly match is diffed word by word, and only the changed words are marked.
6. Everything else in the run is shown as all the old blocks, then all the new ones, so a rewritten section reads as "before, after" instead of alternating.
7. A code block, table, HTML block, or frontmatter can't hold inline marks. When one changes it's shown under a label ("Old table", "New table"), old then new. HTML and frontmatter are shown as code, because MDXEditor can't render them.

Marking blocks one at a time keeps the marks from breaking markdown syntax, e.g. by ending up in the middle of a table row.

Within a block, words are whitespace-separated chunks, so every mark starts and ends next to whitespace, which keeps it valid markdown (`~~ word~~` would not be). A changed region grows into its neighbors until it's balanced on both sides, so a mark never splits `**bold**`, `` `code` ``, or `[link](url)`: changing a link's URL marks the whole link. If more than half the words changed, the block is shown as deleted + inserted instead.

This lives in `src/shared/mdmerge.ts`. It's a pure function, so it has unit tests, and Storybook can call it on fixtures directly.

Every markdown file has a **Rendered / Source** toggle. Source shows the plain markdown diff in Monaco.

### Risks

- A document that already uses `~~` or `==` will look like it has changes. That's rare enough to accept.
- If MDXEditor still fails to parse something, the view falls back to the source diff in Monaco.
- A removed or added table or code block is only marked by its label; the block itself isn't tinted.
- Checked in Storybook: the marks render cleanly, so we don't need the fallback of rendering `<ins>`/`<del>` HTML ourselves.

# Discovery

pridm builds its list of deltas from two sources and joins them on `id`, then attaches Dormouse surfaces.

## 1. Local worktrees

For each clone found under `scanRoots` (e.g. `~/projects`):

1. `git remote get-url origin` gives the origin, which is normalized into the `RepoKey`.
2. `git worktree list --porcelain` gives each worktree's path, head commit, and branch.
3. The base is the merge-base of `HEAD` and `origin/<default branch>`. The default branch comes from `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, falling back to `main`, then `master`.
4. Worktrees with no changes compared with their base are skipped, so a clean `main` checkout doesn't show up.

## 2. Your open PRs

`gh search prs` can't return branch names, and we need those to build ids. So use one GraphQL query through `gh api graphql`, searching `is:pr is:open author:@me`. For each PR it returns: number, title, url, author, draft or not, updatedAt, `headRefName`, `headRefOid`, `baseRefName`, `baseRefOid`, and the repository.

## 3. Join

A PR and a worktree with the same `id` (`<origin>:<branch>`) become one `BulkDelta`. If the PR's base differs from the merge-base, the PR's base wins.

## 4. Where the diff comes from

Both sources sit behind one interface: list the changed files with their +/− counts, and load both versions of one file.

- **Local git** handles local deltas, and PR-only deltas whose repo is cloned under `scanRoots`. For a PR-only delta it first runs `git fetch origin pull/<n>/head`.
  - Changed files: `git diff --numstat -M <base>` and `git diff --name-status -M <base>`.
  - New files git doesn't track yet: `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, because `git diff` leaves them out.
  - Uncommitted files: anything not in `git diff --name-only <base> HEAD`.
  - Contents: `git show <base>:<old path>` for the old version; the file on disk (local) or `git show <head>:<path>` (PR) for the new one.
- **GitHub API** handles PRs with no local clone: `gh api repos/<o>/<r>/pulls/<n>/files` for the file list, and the contents endpoint with the raw media type for the contents. This is the first thing to cut if we're short on time.

## 5. Dormouse surfaces

pridm runs inside Dormouse. `dor list --json --all` lists every surface in the window, each with `id`, `kind`, `title`, `command`, `cwd`, `url`, `activity`, `ringing`, `todo`, and `workspace_id`.

- Terminals and tools match a delta when their `cwd` is its `local.path` or a folder inside it. The longest matching path wins, so worktrees inside the main clone get their own surfaces.
- Browsers match when their `url` starts with the PR's URL.
- `needsAttention` is `ringing || todo`. The dashboard puts deltas where an agent is waiting on you at the top.

pridm itself runs as a Dormouse surface: `dor ensure -- bun run dev`, then `dor agent-browser open surface:N`.

# Data model

The full model is in [`src/types.ts`](../../src/types.ts).

## `BulkDelta`

The root type is a `BulkDelta`: a set of changes on a branch compared with its base. A change doesn't have to be a PR yet:

| Has a local checkout | Has a PR | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yes | no | a worktree you're hacking in, or one an agent is working in |
| no | yes | a PR you opened from another machine, not checked out here |
| yes | yes | the usual case |

```ts
interface BulkDelta {
  id: DeltaId;               // "github.com/owner/repo:branch"
  repo: RepoKey;             // "github.com/owner/repo"
  branch: string | null;     // null = detached HEAD
  base: { ref: string; sha: string };
  title: string;             // PR title, else the last commit subject, else the branch name

  local: LocalCheckout | null;   // path, head commit, uncommitted counts, commits not yet pushed
  pr: PullRequest | null;        // number, url, state, headSha
  surfaces: SurfaceRef[];        // Dormouse panes working on it (live, never saved)

  source: 'local' | 'pr';    // where the diff comes from
}
```

## Decisions

- **The id stays the same when a PR is opened.** It's `<origin>:<branch>`, so a local-only delta and its later PR are the same entry, and focus settings (pinned or muted) carry over.
- **The origin is the normalized `origin` remote URL:** host and path, with no scheme, user, or `.git`. Both `git@github.com:owner/repo.git` and `https://github.com/owner/repo.git` become `github.com/owner/repo`. A clone with no origin uses `file:<path of the main clone>`. Detached HEAD uses `<origin>@<worktree path>` as its id.
- **The local checkout wins when both exist.** The diff comes from the working tree, so it includes uncommitted edits and commits you haven't pushed. `FileStat.committed` marks changes that exist only on disk. `local.upstream.ahead` says the PR is behind your local branch.
- **Choosing the base:** if there's a PR, use its base branch. Otherwise use the merge-base with `origin/<default branch>`.
- **Surfaces are live data.** They're rebuilt from `dor list` on every refresh and never saved.

## Saved state

`~/.pridm/state.json` (`PridmState`) is written by pridm. It holds focus per delta (pinned, normal, muted) and `scanRoots`, the folders to look in for clones.

Category globs are in a separate file, `~/.pridm/categories.json`, because you edit that one by hand. See [Categories](categories.md).

## Known gaps

- PRs from two forks with the same branch name (e.g. `patch-1`) get the same id. That's fine while we only show your own PRs.

# Implementation plan

Written 2026-11-05, for a 2-hour hackathon.

## The demo

One real worktree opens in pridm. Its changes are split into collapsed categories, each with +/− counts. Expanding **spec** shows a rendered markdown diff with changes marked inline. Expanding **prod** shows an inline Monaco diff. The dashboard shows the Claude session working in that worktree.

Everything below serves that demo. The order puts the riskiest part (markdown diff rendering) first, and keeps a working demo possible at the end of each phase.

## Phases

| # | Phase | Time | Ends with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Set up the project | 10 min | Vite app and Storybook both running in Dormouse panes |
| 1 | Diff viewers | 30 min | Markdown and code diff stories that look right in light and dark |
| 2 | Delta view | 15 min | A delta with collapsed categories, in Storybook |
| 3 | Server | 30 min | `/api` returns real deltas from `~/projects` |
| 4 | Wire it up | 15 min | The demo works end to end |
| 5 | Polish | 10 min | Dashboard sorting, Dormouse surfaces, screenshots |

Phases 1–2 (UI, on fixtures) and phase 3 (server) only share `src/types.ts`, so they can be built at the same time, e.g. by a second agent in its own git worktree.

### 0. Set up the project (10 min)

- Vite + React + TypeScript, with Bun as the package manager.
- Install Monaco, MDXEditor, Primer, `picomatch`, `diff`, `mdast-util-from-markdown`.
- Set up Storybook for React + Vite, with a light/dark toggle in the toolbar.
- Move `src/types.ts` into the layout from [Stack](stack.md#project-layout).
- Start both in their own Dormouse panes with `dor ensure -- bun run dev` and `dor ensure -- bun run storybook`.

### 1. Diff viewers (30 min)

The riskiest part goes first. See [Diffs](architecture/diffs.md).

1. `src/shared/mdmerge.ts` with unit tests: block diff, then word diff, then `~~`/`==` marks. Test cases: a word changed, a heading renamed, a list item added, a block deleted, a code block changed, a table changed.
2. `MarkdownDiffView`: read-only MDXEditor plus CSS for the marks. Stories for every test case above.
3. `CodeDiffView`: Monaco `DiffEditor` inline, unchanged regions folded, sized to its content, mounted when it scrolls into view. Stories: added, deleted, modified, renamed, binary, a large file.
4. `theme.ts`: Primer variables, a Monaco theme from Primer's diff colors, light and dark.

**Check:** open the markdown stories with `dor agent-browser` and take screenshots in light and dark. If the marks look bad, switch to the fallback in [Diffs](architecture/diffs.md#risks) now, not later.

### 2. Delta view (15 min)

- `CategoryCounts`: each category's +/− as one line of text, for the dashboard.
- `CategorySection`: `<details>` with the category name, file count, and +/−. When expanded, it shows a list of `CodeDiffView`/`MarkdownDiffView`.
- `DeltaView`: a header (title, branch, PR, uncommitted and unpushed counts) and one section per category.

# Stack

React + TypeScript, built with Vite and run with Bun. React is required because MDXEditor is a React component.

## Libraries

- **Vite** serves the frontend and the `/api` routes, through a small plugin in the dev server. That's one process on one port, so one `dor ensure -- bun run dev`.
- **The server is long-lived.** One instance serves every project and stays running in its own Dormouse pane. `dor ensure` reuses it instead of starting a second one. We don't declare it as a Dor Tool.
- **`@monaco-editor/react`** for `DiffEditor`. It loads Monaco from a CDN by default, so there's no worker setup.
- **`@mdxeditor/editor`** in read-only rich-text mode for markdown.
- **`picomatch`** for category globs.
- **`diff`** (jsdiff) for the markdown merge.
- **`mdast-util-from-markdown`** to split markdown into blocks. MDXEditor already depends on it.
- **Storybook** (`@storybook/react-vite`). See [Storybook](ui/storybook.md).
- **Primer** (`@primer/primitives`, `@primer/octicons-react`, `@primer/react`). See [Design](ui/design.md).
- **`bun test`** for unit tests.

## Project layout

```
vite.config.ts             includes the /api plugin
.storybook/
src/
  types.ts                 the data model, shared by server and UI
  shared/                  pure code, used by both the server and the UI
    mdmerge.ts             builds the merged markdown (tested)
    classify.ts            puts paths into categories (tested)
    overview.ts            groups files into DeltaOverview / CategoryDiff (tested)
    language.ts            Monaco language ids by file extension
  server/
    api.ts                 Vite plugin with the /api routes
    exec.ts                run git / gh / dor and parse output
    origin.ts              normalize remote URLs into RepoKeys
    categories.ts          load categories.json
    state.ts               read and write ~/.pridm/state.json
    discover.ts            worktrees + PRs → BulkDelta[]
    surfaces.ts            dor list → SurfaceRef[] per delta
    sources/
      git.ts               file list and contents from a local clone
      github.ts            file list and contents from the GitHub API
  ui/
    App.tsx                hash routing: dashboard, delta
    hooks.ts               fetch from /api
    theme.ts               Primer setup, Monaco theme, light/dark
    monaco.ts              bundles the local monaco-editor and its workers
    components/            CategoryCounts, CategorySection, CodeDiffView, FileDiffView,
                           MarkdownDiffView, DeltaRow, DeltaView, SurfaceChips
    fixtures/              typed example data for stories
      real/self.json       pridm's own history as a delta; `bun run fixture:self`
scripts/
  fixture-self.ts          builds real/self.json with the server's git code
test/
```

## API

| Route | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/deltas` | `DeltaSummary[]` |
| `GET /api/deltas/:id` | `DeltaOverview` |
| `GET /api/deltas/:id/:category` | `CategoryDiff` |
| `PUT /api/focus/:id` | sets `pinned`, `normal`, or `muted` |

Ids contain `/` and `:`, so they're URL-encoded.

## Pitfalls

- Each Monaco `DiffEditor` is two editors, so an expanded category with many files gets heavy. Mount each one only when it scrolls into view.
- Monaco needs an explicit height. Size each editor to its content.
- MDXEditor needs its stylesheet imported (`@mdxeditor/editor/style.css`) and a plugin for every kind of block it should render: headings, lists, quotes, tables, code blocks, links, thematic breaks, frontmatter.

# Design

GitHub's Primer design system, because your eyes are already trained on GitHub's diffs.

- **`@primer/primitives`** for colors, spacing, and type as CSS variables, including GitHub's diff colors. Light and dark follow the system setting.
- **`@primer/octicons-react`** for icons: file, git-branch, PR, terminal.
- **`@primer/react`** only for a few pieces (`Label`, `CounterLabel`, `Button`, `PageLayout`). Most of the UI is `<details>` sections and editors.

## One set of diff colors

By default Monaco and MDXEditor each have their own idea of what "added" and "removed" look like. Instead:

- Monaco gets a custom theme built from Primer's diff colors (`diffEditor.insertedTextBackground` and so on).
- The CSS for MDXEditor's `==insert==` and `~~delete~~` marks reads the same Primer variables.

So a deletion looks the same in code and in a spec. Monaco (`vs`/`vs-dark`) and MDXEditor (its `dark-theme` class) switch to dark together with Primer.

## Categories

Categories have no colors. Red and green are kept for removed and added, and categories are told apart by their names.

- A category section's header is its name, file count, and +/−.
- A dashboard row lists each category's +/− as text: `spec +120 −14 · prod +88 −31 · test +40 −2`.

# Storybook

Every component is shown in Storybook (`@storybook/react-vite`) in all of its relevant states.

This works because components only take data as props, and fetching happens in a thin layer of hooks above them. Stories are fed fixtures typed with [`src/types.ts`](../../src/types.ts), so they never need a server, git, or `gh`.

## States to cover

- **Dashboard row:** local only, PR only, both; uncommitted changes; local commits not pushed; pinned and muted; a surface that needs attention; one category empty.
- **Category counts:** the default categories, a single category, a custom category, many categories, an empty delta.
- **Category section:** collapsed (totals only), expanded with every file collapsed, loading, a custom category.
- **File diff:** collapsed, expanded, loading.
- **Code diff:** added, deleted, modified, renamed, binary, a large file.
- **Markdown diff:** a word changed in a paragraph, a heading renamed, a list item added, a block deleted, a code block changed, a table changed.
- **All of the above in light and dark,** switched from the Storybook toolbar.

The markdown diff stories are also how we check early that the `~~`/`==` approach renders well. They're the first stories to write.

## Running it

Storybook runs as its own Dormouse surface: `dor ensure -- bun run storybook`. Stories can be opened with `dor agent-browser` and screenshotted to check each state.

# Viewing a delta

A delta opens with every category collapsed. A collapsed category shows only its name, file count, and +/−. You can expand any number of categories at once.

```
feat/inline-md-diffs  ·  github.com/diffplug/pridm#42  ·  2 uncommitted
▸ spec    3 files   +120  −14
▸ prod    5 files    +88  −31
▸ test    2 files    +40   −2
▸ other   1 file      +1   −1
```

Expanding a category lists every one of its files, each collapsed to a single row with its path and +/−. Expanding a file shows its diff, and any number of files can be open at once. See [Diffs](../architecture/diffs.md) for how each kind of file is shown.

## What loads when

The UI loads data in three levels, each only when needed:

1. **`DeltaSummary[]`, for the dashboard:** per-category counts for every delta.
2. **`DeltaOverview`, when you open a delta:** the per-category counts, and each category's file list. Both come from `git diff --numstat`, so this is cheap.
3. **`CategoryDiff`, when you expand a category:** both full versions of every file, plus the merged markdown for markdown files. This is the expensive part, and nobody pays for it in categories that stay collapsed.

Markdown files are counted in **words**, shown as `+105w −686w`, because they're read as rendered text, not lines. Hovering shows the line counts. A category shows words only when every file in it is markdown, so a total never mixes units. The delta's overall total in its header is in lines. Words are whitespace-separated, the same chunks the merged markdown marks; markdown syntax on its own (`##`, `-`, `|`) doesn't count.

## Implementation

- Headers are sticky: while you scroll, the current category's header stays at the top, with the open file's header just under it.
- The sections are plain `<details>`/`<summary>` elements. That gives collapsed by default and expand-several-at-once with no extra code.
- The URL is `#/delta/<id>?open=spec,test`, so a reload or a shared link keeps the same categories open.
- The sections are in the order the origin's categories are written in `categories.json`, with `other` last. Categories with no changed files are left out.

## Dashboard

One row per delta, sorted by: pinned first, then deltas with a surface that needs attention, then most recently updated. Muted deltas go to the bottom. Each row shows:

- the title, branch, and PR number if there is one
- each category's +/−, e.g. `spec +120 −14 · prod +88 −31`
- uncommitted and unpushed counts
- the Dormouse surfaces working on it, e.g. "claude (waiting on you) · npm run dev · browser"
- buttons to pin or mute
